review.translation: [Then|0] [all|1] [flesh|2] [that moved about|3] [on|4] [the earth|5] [died|0], [including the birds|6] [and the livestock|7] [and the wild animals|8] [and all|9] [the swarming creatures|10] [that swarmed|11] [on|12] [the earth|13], [and all|14] [humankind|15].

draft.change: Add a root article for גוע with the Qal sense ‘to die’.
draft.definition: To die, of a person or an animal.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:17 predicts that the creatures with the breath of life will perish. Genesis 7:21–22 recounts the fulfillment, using גוע and then מוּת of those who died.

analysis.evidence: The singular verb agrees with the collective subject כָּל־בָּשָׂר, “all flesh,” which the verse expands to include animals and humans. Genesis 7:22 confirms the sense with מֵתוּ, “they died.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל בָּשָׂר, “all flesh,” כָּל quantifies the collective noun בָּשָׂר. The verse lists birds, livestock, wild animals, swarming creatures, and humans to show whom “all flesh” includes.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל בָּשָׂר is the subject of וַיִּגְוַע, “perished.” The verse specifies which creatures perished by listing birds, livestock, wild animals, swarming creatures, and finally וְכֹל הָאָדָם, “and all humankind.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: In כָּל־בָּשָׂר הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל־הָאָרֶץ, the participle agrees with the singular collective בָּשָׂר and describes what all flesh does on the earth. The following list includes birds, livestock, wild animals, swarming creatures, and humans, supporting the broad sense of movement.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, modifying בָּשָׂר.

analysis.evidence: In הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “that moves on the earth,” עַל introduces the surface on which the creatures move.
In הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “that moves on the ground,” עַל identifies the ground as the surface on which the creatures move.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, common gender, singular absolute

analysis.evidence: בָּעוֹף begins the list of groups included in כָּל בָּשָׂר, “all flesh,” that perished. The parallel phrases וּבַבְּהֵמָה and וּבַחַיָּה name livestock and wild animals, confirming that עוֹף likewise denotes a group.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, realized as בָּ before ע, followed by a masculine singular absolute collective noun.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists וּבַבְּהֵמָה alongside בָּעוֹף ‘among the birds’ and וּבַחַיָּה ‘and among the wild animals’. The separate mention of wild animals identifies בְּהֵמָה here as livestock.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ + preposition בְּ־ with the definite article (בַּ־) + feminine singular absolute noun, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists the creatures that died. וּבַחַיָּה follows וּבַבְּהֵמָה (“and among the livestock”), distinguishing wild animals from livestock within that list.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ + preposition בְּ with the definite article + feminine singular absolute noun, used collectively.
analysis.sense: wild beast, beast of the field

analysis.evidence: In וּבְכָל הַשֶּׁרֶץ, כָל governs the definite collective noun הַשֶּׁרֶץ. The phrase includes all the creatures that swarm on the earth in the list of those that died.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + preposition בְּ־ ‘among’ + masculine singular construct noun כָל.

draft.change: Add the root שרצ with the collective noun שֶׁרֶץ and its related Qal verb שָׁרַץ.
draft.definition: Living creatures that swarm, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 1:20, שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה names the swarm of living creatures with which the waters are to teem.

analysis.evidence: The following participle הַשֹּׁרֵץ agrees with the singular noun. Together with עַל הָאָרֶץ, it identifies the creatures as those that swarm on the earth. They form one group in the verse’s list of living things that died.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
analysis.sense: Living creatures that swarm, taken collectively.

draft.change: Include the Qal sense with creatures as subject alongside the previously proposed sense with waters as subject and the related collective noun.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:21 describes the creatures by their activity on the ground. Genesis 1:20 uses the same verb with the waters as subject.

analysis.evidence: In הַשֶּׁרֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל הָאָרֶץ, the participle agrees in definiteness, gender, and number with the collective noun הַשֶּׁרֶץ. The creatures themselves swarm, and עַל הָאָרֶץ tells where they do so.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used attributively.

analysis.evidence: In הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “that swarms on the ground,” עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ and indicates where the creatures swarm.
In הַשֶּׁרֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל הָאָרֶץ, the phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ identifies the surface on which the creatures swarm.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a singular absolute common noun of common gender.

analysis.evidence: In וְכֹל הָאָדָם, הָאָדָם denotes humankind collectively. The phrase means “and all humankind” and completes the list of those who died.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: וְכֹל הָאָדָם means “and all humankind.” It closes the list of living creatures included in כָּל בָּשָׂר (“all flesh”) that perished.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
